topic: Point Nemo (48°52.6′S 123°23.6′W), the oceanic pole of inaccessibility, lies about 2,688 km from the nearest land (Ducie Island, Motu Nui, Maher Island); the ISS orbits at about 400 km, so its crew are at times the nearest humans; the surrounding area is used as the 'spacecraft cemetery' where 260+ spacecraft including Mir were deorbited.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.reality: It is a point of open ocean, the spot farthest from any coastline; there is no land there at all.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

screen_exempt: ^A was right|^B was right|^C was right

landscape.our_gap: Point Nemo Shorts are narrated stock-footage clips about 'the creepiest place on Earth'; nobody draws the 2,688 km circle to scale on the satellite map, pins the three specks, and ties the orbit altitude to the spacecraft cemetery in one minute.

existing.title: Point Nemo, the most remote place on Earth

noaa.title: What is Point Nemo?
noaa.notes: Oceanic pole of inaccessibility at 48°52.6′S 123°23.6′W; about 2,688 km from the nearest land (Ducie Island, Motu Nui, Maher Island); used for controlled re-entries of spacecraft.

lukatela.title: A Point of Inaccessibility in the Pacific Ocean (1992 computation)
lukatela.notes: Original computation: 48°52.6′S 123°23.6′W, 2,688 km from Ducie Island, Motu Nui and Maher Island.

wiki_nemo.title: Pole of inaccessibility — Oceanic pole (Point Nemo)
wiki_nemo.notes: Point Nemo, 2,688 km from the three nearest islands; ISS crews at ~400 km are at times the nearest humans; spacecraft cemetery nearby.

wiki_cemetery.title: Spacecraft cemetery
wiki_cemetery.notes: South Pacific Ocean Uninhabited Area around Point Nemo; between 1971 and 2016 at least 263 spacecraft were deorbited there, including Mir (2001).

esa.title: Where do old satellites go when they die? (Space debris)
esa.notes: Controlled re-entries target the South Pacific Ocean Uninhabited Area, far from shipping and land.

nasa_iss.title: International Space Station facts and figures
nasa_iss.notes: The ISS orbits at an average altitude of about 400 km (250 miles).

brit_mir.title: Mir (space station)
brit_mir.notes: Mir was deorbited on 23 March 2001 over the South Pacific.

popsci.title: The spacecraft cemetery at Point Nemo
popsci.notes: More than 260 spacecraft, including Mir, brought down in the uninhabited South Pacific area around Point Nemo.

claims.text: Point Nemo, the oceanic pole of inaccessibility (48°52.6′S 123°23.6′W), is about 2,688 km from the nearest land.
vo: this is point nemo, the spot in the south pacific farthest from any land. the nearest coast is 2,688 kilometres away
the loneliest point in the ocean, where the only neighbours pass by in orbit
screen: closer than any coast at 2,688 km

claims.text: The three nearest pieces of land are Ducie Island (Pitcairn), Motu Nui (off Easter Island) and Maher Island (Antarctica), all uninhabited.
vo: three specks of land sit on that circle: ducie island to the north, motu nui off easter island to the north-east, and maher island, on the edge of antarctica, to the south
nobody lives on any of them

claims.text: The ISS orbits at about 400 km, so when it passes over Point Nemo its crew are nearer than anyone on land.
vo: there is a point in the ocean where the nearest human beings are usually in orbit
the space station passes about 400 kilometres overhead, so when it does, its crew are the closest people to this spot
screen: The place where the nearest people are in space

claims.text: The area around Point Nemo is used for controlled spacecraft re-entries; at least 263 spacecraft were deorbited there between 1971 and 2016, including Mir in 2001.
vo: that emptiness is useful. space agencies steer dead spacecraft to burn up and fall here, more than 250 of them so far, including the mir space station
